Let nX denote the number of atoms of element X per hydrogen atom in a stellar photosphere.

Solar reference abundances (given)
 12 + log10(nFe⊙/nH) = 7.5  ⇒  log10(nFe⊙/nH) = –4.5
 12 + log10(nMg⊙/nH) = 7.0  ⇒  log10(nMg⊙/nH) = –5.0
 (no solar Si value is needed explicitly; ratios suffice)

----------------------------------------------------------
Star 1
[Fe/H]₁ = 0 dex  ⇒  nFe₁ / nH = nFe⊙ / nH

[Si/Fe]₁ = 0.3 dex
   [Si/Fe] = log10[(nSi/nFe)/(nSi/nFe)⊙]
   ⇒ (nSi/nFe)₁ = 10^{0.3} (nSi/nFe)⊙

Hence nSi₁ = (nSi/nFe)₁ · nFe₁
            = 10^{0.3} (nSi/nFe)⊙ · nFe⊙
            = 10^{0.3} nSi⊙                        (1)

----------------------------------------------------------
Star 2
[Mg/H]₂ = 0 dex  ⇒  nMg₂ / nH = nMg⊙ / nH

[Mg/Si]₂ = 0.3 dex
   [Mg/Si] = log10[(nMg/nSi)/(nMg/nSi)⊙]
   ⇒ (nMg/nSi)₂ = 10^{0.3} (nMg/nSi)⊙

Therefore nSi₂ = nMg₂ /(nMg/nSi)₂
               = nMg⊙ /(10^{0.3} · (nMg/nSi)⊙ )
               = nSi⊙ · 10^{–0.3}                 (2)

----------------------------------------------------------
Ratio of silicon atoms
From (1) and (2):

  nSi₁ / nSi₂ = [nSi⊙ · 10^{0.3}] / [nSi⊙ · 10^{–0.3}]
              = 10^{0.3 + 0.3}
              = 10^{0.6} ≈ 3.98 ≈ 3.9

----------------------------------------------------------
Thus the photosphere of Star 1 contains about four times as many silicon atoms per hydrogen atom as that of Star 2.

Answer: D
